title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and 100 other companies call for action to defend against rogue AI
slides: They just signed a joint safety pledge.
But the pledge has zero enforcement power.
Your AI tools may soon change compliance rules.
Audit your own AI systems this week.
thread_text:
1. Who stops rogue AI?

100 companies signed a pledge. But it has zero enforcement power. Nothing changes unless you audit your own systems.

2. The pledge's hidden catch

Compliance rules are about to shift. Your AI tools may need to meet new standards. Are you ready?

3. Audit before it's required

Regulators are watching. A self-audit this week can prevent future penalties. Don't wait for the mandate.

4. What your AI hides

Most systems have invisible biases. The pledge ignores them. Only a deep dive reveals the risks.

5. Your move this week

Run a prompt on your AI, check for bias. If you haven't audited yet, start now. Does it pass?

instagram.caption:
100 companies—OpenAI, Anthropic, Google included—just signed a safety pledge against rogue AI, but it’s purely symbolic.  

No enforcement power, no penalties. The document commits them to “responsible” development, but nothing forces them to change a line of code. Regulators are now watching closer, and your compliance rules will likely shift because of this pressure.  

What changes for you: if you use any AI tools in your content pipeline, expect new auditing standards sooner than later. Self-audit your systems this week before a mandate lands on your desk.  

Does your current AI pass a basic bias check you run today? 🧠⚖️🛠️
